title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>DoorDash reduced grocery reorder latency from 16 to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchase needs using batch LLM inference and deterministic validation. Live catalog resolution keeps product selections current, while an editable shopping interface avoids unnecessary model calls. The company reports that shopping list views doubled and the flow’s order rate increased by approximately 34%</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-gpu-distributed-systems/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576903003.jpg"/><p>Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: The Ladder Is Missing Rungs: Engineering Progression When AI Ate the Middle
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-software-engineering-pipeline/en/mediumimage/alasdair-allan-medium-1791451156021.jpeg"/><p>Alasdair Allan discusses empirical research from METR and Anthropic on AI coding adoption. He explains the "supervision paradox," where reliance on AI tools disrupts junior skill development, risks institutional context loss, and threatens the long-term engineering pipeline needed to oversee autonomous systems effectively.</p> <i>By Alasdair Allan</i>

title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-titus-kubernetes-microvm/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793268697529.jpg"/><p>Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Article: InfoQ AI, ML and Data Engineering Trends Report - 2026
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/ai-ml-data-engineering-trends-2026/en/headerimage/ai-ml-de-graph-2026-1793191771570.jpg"/><p>This InfoQ Trends Report offers readers a comprehensive overview of emerging trends and technologies in the areas of AI, ML, and Data Engineering. This report summarizes the InfoQ editorial team’s and external guests' view on the current trends in AI and ML technologies and what to look out for in the next 12 months.</p> <i>By Srini Penchikala, Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals</i>

title: Podcast: AI, ML, and Data Engineering InfoQ Trends Report 2026
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/ai-ml-data-engineering-trends-2026/en/smallimage/trend-reports-thumbnail-1793181579584.jpg"/><p>In this episode, members of the InfoQ AI and ML editorial staff and friends of InfoQ discuss the current trends in the domain of AI, ML and Data Engineering. One of the regular features of InfoQ are the trends reports, which each focus on a different aspect of software dev. These reports provide the InfoQ readers and listeners with a high-level overview of the topics to pay attention to this year.</p> <i>By Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals</i>

title: Microsoft Retires Azure Deployment Environments with No Replacement Product
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ade-dev-box-retirement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792499241111.jpg"/><p>Azure Deployment Environments retires on February 22, 2027 and Microsoft names no successor, telling teams to use Bicep or ARM templates directly. Microsoft Dev Box follows on September 18, 2028, pointed at Windows 365, which Microsoft says is not a one-to-one replacement. Remaining Dev Box workloads should expect deletion.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/bug0-agent-testing-cached-replay/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793286673185.jpg"/><p>QA Agent is a new source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The agent associates test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on multi-model consensus and vision model evaluations.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: How to Make Artificial Intelligence More Environmentally Sustainable
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/AI-environmentally-sustainable/en/headerimage/header-1793174464846.jpg"/><p>IT is responsible for about 2 - 4% of all global emissions, and electricity use at Microsoft and Google has climbed because of AI, according to their own reports. Sustainability ought to be a top-level architectural concern. Some recommendations are: use pre-built and smaller models, run compute where low-carbon electricity is abundant, and train on renewable energy.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-pc-picks/en/headerimage/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-pc-picks-1793192613417.jpg"/><p>Who authorizes an agent’s actions, and how should teams manage growing context costs? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee shares six session picks that tackle these questions, alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: Anthropic Says Nobody Needs a Mental Model of Claude Code. Practitioners Are Testing That
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/anthropic-code-review/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792959100117.jpg"/><p>Anthropic has published how the Claude Code team reviews code now that Claude writes roughly 90% of it, including a claim that nobody keeps a complete mental model of the codebase. The post documents a pull request that ran more than fifty review rounds overnight, a reviewer spending most of its effort on pre-existing code, and a control the team says it does not yet have.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/datadog-scout-sre-model/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793038066919.jpg"/><p>Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-web-search-api/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791616850849.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has recently launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway. Available through REST APIs and Cloudflare Workers, it provides unified logging, access controls, and billing, and supports bring-your-own-provider keys.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Airbnb extended its Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real-Time Model Transform to update sequence-based recommendation embeddings within seconds. The architecture reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to under a minute and improved offline NDCG by 1.67%, while online testing increased uncancelled bookings by approximately one-third of a percent.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>
